Steady drizzle in Wellington on Friday forced New Zealand to shift their training to an indoor facility opposite the Basin Reserve, while India cancelled their training session and stayed back at their hotel on the eve of the second ODI of the five-match series on Saturday.The turnaround time between the Auckland and Wellington fixtures permitted only one practice session for both teams following their travel day on November 5. While players who were part of India's T20I set-up have already had a taste of the windy Welly, most will walk straight into action, hoping to acclimatise quickly. New Zealand poses stiff challenges, and the varying ground dimensions and weather conditions across the country present different hurdles to overcome.From the short straight at Eden Park to the shorter square at Hnry Stadium, even the bowlers from both teams will need to make that quick adjustment because what worked in Auckland may or may not reap rewards in Wellington. For Kiwi quick Blair Tickner, it's about getting the work done in whatever time you get and finding the right balance between fixtures."We still do a bit of bowling between. You can't do it every time, there's guys going in and out of the session and we're just balancing that, and a lot of guys going to Test cricket as well, so there's a lot of balance happening.We have a great team and they are all sort of scheduling each bowler where they need to be, so now it's working so far, so good," said Tickner on the cramped schedule."I'm still coming back from a few injuries in the winter, so I'm sort of trying to bowl a bit more. I love bowling, getting that rhythm right, so I'm definitely still bowling in training and getting me to it," added the fast bowler, who flexed his muscles by smashing four massive sixes in Auckland.Tickner enjoyed putting on a show for the crowd but now wants to put up an improved performance with the ball at a venue where Abhishek Sharma blew the hosts away with a 38-ball 113. With lessons learnt, New Zealand will continue to come hard at India, and attack will be the mantra for the hosts."If the perfect plan works out, we are going to be attacking and get early wickets. That's the dream, and every one day team's bowling attack wants to bowl teams out, so we're looking to bowl teams out first before thinking about defensive play. We'll work it out there," said Tickner.India will have to decide whether to bench Nabi to make way for Siraj, who joined the team after finishing his India A duties. The experienced fast bowler linked up with the squad in Wellington and remains available for selection. A practice session could have offered hints about the team management's thinking, but fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh kept his selection cards close to his chest."Siraj has joined the team and is available for selection, but the management will take a call whether he will play or not," said Ghosh.Given the weather conditions, it looks increasingly difficult for India to alter their bowling combination, and the only toss-up could be between Siraj and Nabi.There is a strong forecast of rain on match day as well, and the fans could be in for another frustrating day of cricket when the two teams take the field.
Article Summary: Weather could play a spoilsport in the second match between New Zealand and India set to be played at the Hnry Stadium in Wellington. The turnaround time between the Auckland and Wellington fixtures permitted only one practice session for both teams following their travel day on November 5. New Zealand will continue to come hard at India, and attack will be the mantra for the hosts.

Article Title: From Siu to see you: Cristiano Ronaldo says goodbye to international football
Article Text:
FILE PHOTO: Soccer Football - Euro 2020 - Group F - Portugal v France - Puskas Arena, Budapest, Hungary - June 23, 2021 Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates scoring their second goal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The iconic 'Siu' celebration will no longer ring out on the international stage. Not all curtain calls are happy spectacles, a packed arena cheering the last hurrah of a performer par excellence. Cristiano Ronaldo had his floodlit moments in the cauldrons of Stade de France, Porto, Gelsenkirchen, Luzhniki, Wembley, the Bernabeu or Munich's Allianz Arena.On Thursday, Portugal's superstar announced his intention to retire from the country's national team in a social media post, bringing an end to one of the most illustrious careers in all football history. "The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team," he wrote in an 866-word message. "I never felt it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world."Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future ... A journey that began in Aug 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end. When I look back at everything with the national team, I don't just see the matches, goals, records or trophies."All expected him to say ‘obrigado’ at Dallas Stadium after Portugal lost to Spain in his last World Cup match on July 6, 2026. It marked his 27th appearance across a record six tournaments (2006-2026), making him the oldest player in a World Cup knockout match at 41.Instead, the Portugal great, if not the greatest, waited for his bete noire Lionel Messi to sail into the twilight at the Monumental Stadium, waited till national coach Jorge Jesus’ royal ignore forced him into an ugly spat, a chase to the airport to coax him back. Of late, Cristiano had been making headlines for the wrong reasons.Images of Cristiano struggling inside the rival penalty box have long overshadowed his overwhelming prowess that made him snatch five Ballons D’Or to Messi’s eight. Their game of one-upmanship spread across two decades leaving the world gasping for more. Gen Z is cleaved down the middle over the Portuguese and the Argentinian. The discourse will take some years to lose steam.No men’s footballer has made as many international appearances (234) or scored as many goals (146) for their nation as Ronaldo. As a testament to his longevity — 94 of them came after his 30th birthday.The five-time Ballon d’Or-winner made his international debut in 2003, and won the 2016 European Championship, in addition to two Nations League titles, with Portugal.Ronaldo scored three goals at this summer’s World Cup as his nation exited in the Round of 16.Recalling his great matches would be an exercise in academic drudgery. The hat-trick against Spain in Sochi in 2018 and the World Cup qualifier goals against Zlatan Ibrahimovic’s Sweden in 2013 are just the tip of the iceberg.So are the moments of irony. In 2012, Luis Nani missed one on a platter offered to him by Cristiano in the Euro semifinal against Spain. Portugal lost. Four years later, Cristiano’s final against France ended in a tear-soaked heartache, injured and substituted after 25 minutes. Portugal went on to win their first continental title.Before Ronaldo, a senior Portugal side had never won anything, had only made the World Cup semifinals twice, in 1966 and 2006 (his first World Cup). With him leading them, they won three trophies in nine years.Madeira, his birthplace, has a museum as a tribute to its most famous son. Like Santos has one for Pele.Accolades will continue to flow and the ‘Siuuu’ celebration will be replicated by boys across the globe for years to come.For now, like Messi, Ronaldo will keep playing at club level, and is expected to finish his club career at the end of this season with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. He is in pursuit of his 1,000th career goal and currently sits on 985. The immortal longings refuse to die.As his goodbye post reads: “Goals fade. Trophies end up in museums. Records are eventually broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we hold in people’s hearts.”
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from the Portugal national team. The five-time Ballon d'Or winner made his international debut in 2003, and won the 2016 European Championship, in addition to two Nations League titles, with Portugal. Ronaldo scored three goals at this summer’s World Cup as his nation exited in the Round of 16.

Article Title: Bangladesh hold their breath: Opener Shadman Islam stretchered off after on-field injury in second Test; hosts risk being reduced to 10 players
Article Text:
Photo/Cricbuzz

Bangladesh opener Shadman Islam was stretchered off the field after twisting his ankle while fielding on the second morning of the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet on Friday.The incident took place in the 78th over of West Indies' first innings when Shadman chased a ball played towards fine leg by Amir Jangoo. The opener slipped while trying to stop the ball and immediately went down in pain near the boundary. He remained on the ground for several minutes before being taken off on a stretcher.Shadman has been taken to hospital for an MRI scan and is currently under observation. A decision on his availability for the remainder of the match will be taken after the scan results.Morning dew had left the outfield wet and slippery near the boundary ropes, The Daily Star reported. Earlier in the day, Bangladesh pacer Hasan Mahmud had also slipped while attempting to stop a delivery."He twisted his left ankle and was taken to hospital for an MRI scan," BCB physio Bayzediul Islam said in a statement.Bangladesh had bowled West Indies out for 356 after lunch on the second day. In Shadman's absence, they sent Nayeem Hasan, who had not batted above No.8 before this match, to open alongside Tanzid Hasan.Shadman had scored a century in the first Test, but it remains unclear whether he will be able to take any further part in the ongoing match.Bangladesh cannot bring in a concussion substitute if Shadman is ruled out because of the ankle injury, which is unrelated to a head injury. This means they would have to continue with only 10 players for the remainder of the Test.West Indies lead the two-match series 1-0.
Article Summary: Bangladesh opener Shadman Islam stretchered off the field after twisting his ankle while fielding on the second morning of the second Test against West Indies. The incident took place in the 78th over of West Indies' first innings when Shadman chased a ball played towards fine leg by Amir Jangoo. The opener slipped while trying to stop the ball and immediately went down in pain near the boundary.

Article Title: 15-year-old Tanvi Patri scripts history, becomes first Indian woman to win Youth Olympics badminton medal
Article Text:
Tanvi Patri (Image credit: BAI)

A fightback that nearly produced gold

Tanvi Patri's road to the Youth Olympics final

Quarterfinal: A historic semifinal entry

Semifinal: Tanvi holds her nerve against Japan's second seed

Joins elite company of Indian badminton medallists

At just 15, Odisha's Tanvi Patri becomes the first Indian woman to win a badminton medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Her remarkable silver-medal run in Dakar was a story of composure, courage and extraordinary fighting spirit, highlighted by a stunning comeback in the final against China's reigning World Junior Champion Zhang Yi Xin.India's Tanvi Patri scripted a historic chapter in Indian badminton after clinching the silver medal in the women's singles event at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. The 15-year-old from Odisha became the first Indian woman to reach a badminton final and win a medal at the Youth Olympics, marking a significant milestone for the country's junior badminton circuit.However, the road to the podium was anything but straightforward. Tanvi's campaign was defined by her ability to rise to the occasion, particularly in the knockout stages, where she displayed remarkable composure against some of the tournament's strongest opponents.The young shuttler eventually settled for silver after an 82-minute battle against China's reigning World Junior Champion Zhang Yi Xin in the gold-medal match. Tanvi went down 15-21, 21-13, 24-26 in a thrilling three-game encounter, but her spirited fightback in the deciding game ensured that her performance would be remembered long after the final point.The final against Zhang was a test of Tanvi's temperament and endurance. After losing the opening game 15-21, the Indian bounced back impressively to take the second game 21-13 and force a decider.The third game, however, appeared to be slipping away from her when she found herself trailing 10-19. With the gold medal seemingly within Zhang's grasp, Tanvi produced an extraordinary response, refusing to surrender despite the mounting pressure.She saved five consecutive match points to draw level at 24-24, turning what looked like a comfortable finish for the Chinese shuttler into a tense battle. Tanvi even earned three opportunities to seal the gold medal herself, but Zhang held her nerve in the closing exchanges to eventually prevail 26-24.Although the defeat denied her the gold, Tanvi's determination to fight until the very end stood out as one of the defining moments of the tournament.The 15-year-old, who trains at the Prakash Padukone Badminton Academy (PPBA), entered the competition as the third seed and enjoyed a strong start in the group stage.Tanvi faced Thailand's seventh-seeded Kakanik Kungkaew in the quarterfinals, with a place in the medal rounds at stake. The Indian youngster delivered a composed performance, winning 21-17, 21-13 in just 39 minutes. The straight-games victory not only secured her a semifinal berth but also made her the first Indian woman to reach the badminton semifinals at the Youth Olympic Games.The semifinal against Japan's second-seeded Yuzuno Watanabe proved to be a much tougher examination.Tanvi began confidently, taking the opening game 21-14 with an aggressive approach and precise shot-making. However, Watanabe responded strongly in the second game, capitalising on Tanvi's errors to level the contest with a 21-11 win.With a place in the final on the line, the Indian youngster needed to produce her best badminton in the deciding game. She managed to regain control of the rallies, improved her attacking approach and kept her composure in the closing stages.In a closely contested decider, Tanvi edged past Watanabe 21-19 to book her place in the gold-medal match.The victory was another landmark moment, making her the first Indian woman to reach a badminton final at the Youth Olympics.Tanvi's silver medal also adds to India's growing legacy in badminton at the Youth Olympic Games. She joins H.S. Prannoy, who won silver in 2010, and Lakshya Sen, who secured silver in 2018, as Indian badminton players to have reached the podium at the prestigious multi-sport event.More importantly, her achievement marks a first for Indian women's badminton at the tournament.
Article Summary: Odisha's Tanvi Patri becomes the first Indian woman to win a badminton medal at the Youth Olympic Games. The 15-year-old's remarkable silver-medal run in Dakar was a story of composure, courage and extraordinary fighting spirit. She produced a stunning comeback in the final against China's reigning World Junior Champion Zhang Yi Xin.

Article Title: At 93, the battles of Tokyo still live on in Dharam Singh Mann's memory
Article Text:
Action from the 1964 Olympics final between India and Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JALANDHAR: Dharam Singh Mann may have put away his hockey stick decades ago, but his passion for the game remains undiminished. At 93, one of Punjab's oldest surviving links to Indian hockey's golden era, Mann played in the gold-medal-winning team at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics and the bronze-winning side at the 1968 Mexico Games. He vividly remembers the bruises, battles and bonds that shaped his journey.As Jalandhar, the heartland of Indian hockey, hosted the initial rounds of the Asian Champions Trophy, Mann served as a poignant reminder of a glorious legacy the sport must cherish and pass on to future generations.A retired Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with Punjab Police, Mann began his journey on the village grounds, where his first hockey stick was his father's. "I used to take his stick and wait for my turn outside the village ground. The day I got my first chance, there was no looking back," he told TOI.Mann's international journey gathered momentum with the 1963 Lyon International Hockey Tournament in France, a key preparatory event ahead of the Tokyo Olympics. He also suffered a broken jaw after being struck by a rival's stick. He remembers the care he received from hockey legend Udham Singh, who brought him homemade desi ghee-bone broth and fed him for days as he recovered.Despite his age, memories of the 1964 Olympic final against Pakistan refuse to fade. When the old rivals targeted India's centre-forward Harbinder Singh, Mann and teammates Prithipal Singh and Gurbax Singh decided not to let the intimidation go unanswered. "We told him the game wasn't over. We would challenge them on the field like it's war," he recalled with a smile. India eventually prevailed, winning Olympic gold.During a visit to a primary school in Japan, Mann was struck by children who, instead of talking about what they wanted to become, asked what they could do for their country. He believes this sense of collective responsibility was central to Japan's sporting success and carried that lesson into hockey and the Punjab Police.
Article Summary: Dharam Singh Mann is one of Punjab's oldest surviving links to Indian hockey's golden era. Mann played in the gold-medal-winning team at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics and the bronze-winning side at the 1968 Mexico Games. He vividly remembers the bruises, battles and bonds that shaped his journey.

Article Title: First-timer Jaypal Malviya earns LA28 quota in 10m air pistol
Article Text:
Jaypal Malviya

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PUNE: On a day when all eyes on Manu Bhaker to win a medal and a quota place, Jaypal Malviya came unannounced to do the honours at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on Thursday.Madhya Pradesh’s Malviya, who was participating in his first international competition in the medals category, won silver in men’s 10m air pistol event and also booked India's first berth for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.Malviya, 31, scored 242.2 in the final, while China’s Hu Kai shot 243.9 to win gold. Czech Republic’s Jindrich Dubovy took bronze and the third quota place on offer with a score of 220.9.Malviya had entered the final after shooting 585 in the qualification round.Earlier, Manu Bhaker missed on winning a medal and a quota place after finishing fifth in women’s 10m air pistol event. Manu scored 179.9 in the final and a fourth-place finish would have secured at least a quota as there were two Chinese in the top-four and only one athlete from one country gets the quota from one match.Another Indian, Suruchi Singh, met a similar fate as she finished behind Manu with a score of 158.3. Manu had shot 583, while Suruchi had scored 580 to enter the final.In the men’s final, Malviya. the son of a farmer from MP’s Chhindwara district, got off to a modest start with lower 10s and some 9s in between till his first 12 shots. Though he maintained his ranking in the top-5, he changed gears after the 12 shots with 10.6, 10.2, 10.7 and 10.8 to climb up to second position in the 8-shooter final.In the last four rounds, where bronze and gold were decided, Malviya shot two 9.7s and a 10.7 to stay in the hunt, but Kai's 10.6, 10.7 and a 10.5 in the last three shots gave no chance to the Indian for gold.The final had three Chinese shooters, including Paris Games champion Yu Xie and Hu Kai, who had won all the gold medals in the four World Cups last year. The finalists also had Paris Games bronze medallist Paolo Monna of Italy, however, he crashed out of the final at fifth position, while Xie got eliminated at seventh position.“He was playing only in his first international match, that too at the World Championships. He shot really well despite being shaky in the beginning. I feel he controlled his mind well and executed his plan effectively,” India coach and former shooter Samaresh Jung told TOI
Article Summary: Madhya Pradesh's Jaypal Malviya wins silver in men's 10m air pistol event. He also booked India's first berth for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Earlier, Manu Bhaker missed on winning a medal and a quota place.

Article Title: ‘Everybody can play on turf’: Dutch Olympic champion explains where India are falling behind
Article Text:
Floris Jan Bovelander

Mohali:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Netherlands hockey star Floris jan Bovelander believes India’s vast talent pool can only translate into sustained global success if the country improves access to artificial turf pitches and strengthens grassroots development programmes.In Punjab for the Asian Champions Trophy, Bovelander, who has been involved in hockey development projects in India for more than a decade, said the biggest difference between hockey powers such as the Netherlands and India remained infrastructure at the grassroots level.“We have more than a thousand turf pitches in the Netherlands and all kids start on turf pitches,” Bovelander said. “The techniques and tactics of modern hockey are easier to learn when you play on turf from a young age.”While India possesses a far larger playing base, he noted that many pitches remain concentrated in stadiums and elite centres, limiting access for young players.“You have pitches, but sometimes you’re not allowed to play on them because they’re in stadiums. In the Netherlands, everybody can play on the turf pitches. That’s important for development,” said the two-time Olympic gold medallist.Bovelander, who helped establish the Naval Tata Hockey Academy in Jharkhand and remains involved in community-based programmes through the Bovelander Foundation, stressed that infrastructure alone was not enough.“There is often a lot of focus on high performance, but high-performance hockey benefits from strong grassroots programmes,” he added. “You need festivals, school competitions, youth leagues and good coaching. Elite players inspire young children, but you also need a strong base underneath.”As for the Indian men’s team, Bovelander said it had developed into one of the world’s most difficult sides to beat, citing back-to-back Olympic bronze medals as evidence of its progress. However, he admitted India had occasionally fallen short in key moments at major tournaments.“They are one of the top teams in the world. Maybe they are missing a little bit in the key moments, but they are always there,” he said. “If things go their way at one of the next major tournaments, they can win.”Bovelander also called for a healthy balance between experienced players and emerging talent, saying national teams should avoid relying on reputation alone.“Players should be in the team because of their performances, not because of their history,” he said. “Young players must keep pushing the experienced ones.”India’s 2016 Junior World Cup-winning generation had gone on to form the backbone of the senior side, he noted, but the challenge now was ensuring the next crop of youngsters was given similar opportunities.As far as his discussions with Punjab’s administration is concerned, Bovelander said he hoped to explore ways of contributing to coaching and grassroots initiatives, adding that expanding access to playing facilities would be among the issues he would raise with policymakers.
Article Summary: Former Netherlands hockey star Floris jan Bovelander believes India’s vast talent pool can only translate into sustained global success if the country improves access to artificial turf pitches. He has been involved in hockey development projects in India for more than a decade.

Article Title: Kylian Mbappe creates Champions League history, joins Lionel Messi in elite list
Article Text:
Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (AP Photo)

Mbappe milestone as Real Madrid stage comeback against AEK Athens

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe added another milestone to his impressive UEFA Champions League career on Wednesday, becoming the second-fastest player to register 100 goal contributions in the competition's history.The French superstar reached the landmark during Real Madrid's clash against AEK Athens, finding the net in the 78th minute to take his combined tally of goals and assists to 100. Mbappe has now recorded 74 goals and 26 assists in 102 Champions League appearances.Only Lionel Messi reached the milestone quicker, taking 101 matches to register 100 goal contributions. The Argentina great achieved the feat while representing Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) before moving to Major League Soccer (MLS), where he currently plays for Inter Miami.Cristiano Ronaldo remains at the top of the all-time Champions League goal contributions chart with 182, comprising 140 goals and 42 assists.The record-breaking moment came during an eventful encounter in Athens, where Real Madrid had to fight back after falling behind twice before eventually securing a 3-2 victory.AEK Athens made an early breakthrough through Aboubakary Koita, who opened the scoring in the 12th minute following an assist from Luka Jovic.Real Madrid thought they had found an equaliser when Vinicius Jr 's cross ended up in the net following a touch from Jude Bellingham. However, the goal was ruled out because the English midfielder was adjudged to be offside.Bellingham made up for the disallowed effort just three minutes later, producing an excellent backheel finish in the 32nd minute to bring Madrid back into the contest, as reported by Goal.com.Mbappe also had an opportunity to create danger when he picked out an unmarked Marc Cucurella, but the latter failed to make the most of the chance with his weaker foot.The hosts regained the advantage in the 75th minute, with Koita turning provider this time by setting up Stavro Pilo, who put AEK Athens on the verge of a memorable victory.However, Madrid responded almost immediately. Denzel Dumfries delivered a cross that Mbappe converted in the 78th minute, restoring parity while simultaneously bringing up his 100th Champions League goal contribution.With the match heading towards its conclusion, Federico Valverde stepped up with a stunning strike, finding the top corner to complete Madrid's comeback and seal a dramatic 3-2 win.The victory ensured that Mbappe's personal milestone was accompanied by another important result for Real Madrid in Europe.
Article Summary: Kylian Mbappe becomes second-fastest player to register 100 Champions League goal contributions. The French forward reached the landmark during Real Madrid's 3-2 win against AEK Athens on Wednesday. Only Lionel Messi reached the milestone quicker, taking 101 matches to do so.

Article Title: How NBA is looking to turn India into a billion-dollar basketball market
Article Text:
Left to right: Rajah Chaudhry (NBA's Head of Strategy, Asia Pacific), Sunny Malik (Country Head, NBA India), DeMarcus Cousins and Isiah Thomas. (Image: LinkedIn)

FIRST NBA STORE IN INDIA TO OPEN IN 2027 THROUGH EXPANDED MERCHANDISING PARTNERSHIP WITH SUDITI.

For a league that has spent decades turning basketball players into global icons and team jerseys into fashion statements, the NBA 's ambitions in India were never going to be restricted to television screens. The challenge, however, is turning that appeal into a sustainable business.India, with its young population, expanding digital audience and growing appetite for global sports and entertainment, represents a significant long-term opportunity for the league. But the NBA is conscious that building a presence in a cricket-dominated market requires more than securing a broadcaster and hoping fans tune in to watch games played thousands of kilometres and many timezones away.It is looking to create multiple entry points for consumers, with basketball, fashion, music, entertainment and retail forming parts of a larger commercial strategy.The latest step in that direction is the expansion of its merchandising partnership with Indian apparel company Suditi. Having worked together since 2018, the two have extended their association, with Suditi taking over the operation of NBAStore.in in October 2026.The expanded portfolio includes casual shirts and lifestyle footwear, alongside jerseys, T-shirts, jackets, sweatshirts, headwear and accessories.More significantly, the partnership will see the NBA open its first physical store in India in 2027. It is an important development for a league looking to take its relationship with fans beyond digital engagement and into everyday consumption.The idea is to make NBA merchandise a lifestyle proposition rather than limit it to conventional sports apparel. Its teams, players and iconic jerseys already have recognition beyond basketball-following circles. Just look at numerous LA Lakers, Chicago Bulls, Michael Jordan, Steph Curry, LeBron James knockoffs that get sold in the local markets. The opportunity lies in converting that cultural appeal into official merchandise sales.Long-term commercial partnerships are another important part of the NBA's business model. Swiss watchmaker Tissot, which has been associated with the league for a decade, is an example of how these relationships can evolve beyond brand visibility."Our partnerships are built on shared values, a common vision and a commitment to evolving together. The decade-long NBA association exemplifies this, with both brands continually innovating to enhance fan experience, most recently through a redesigned shot clock now adopted across the WNBA," Tissot CEO Sylvain Dolla told TimesofIndia.com.Dolla added that the same approach extended to the brand's associations across basketball, cycling and motorsport, where it works with Swiss Timing to develop sport-specific solutions. "Our objective is to contribute to each sport's growth through long-term collaboration and innovation," he added.But retail and partnerships are only part of the equation.The NBA has spent considerable time experimenting with how Indian audiences consume its product. Its broadcast journey has included a decade-long association with Sony, followed by partnerships with MTV and digital platforms. It also explored making 100 games available live on YouTube, while its three-year association with Prasar Bharati took basketball content to DD Sports and a wider free-to-air audience.The reasoning was straightforward: live games alone cannot drive growth in a market where matches are played at inconvenient hours for Indian viewers."You can't just focus on broadcast and say, 'please watch my game.' You have to do other things around the sport," said Rajah Chaudhry, NBA's Asia-Pacific head of strategy, during an interaction with TimesofIndia.com in June."The objective is not to get cocooned into just one way of saying that live games are the way to be. We want to try different ways because people like to consume games in different ways in the country. That's our objective," added Sunny Malik, NBA India's Country Head.For the 2026-27 season, NBA games are available live in India on Prime Video and NBA League Pass. The challenge is to ensure that audiences remain connected to the league even when they are not watching live action.That is where digital content assumes importance. The NBA's Indian social media platforms have accumulated more than eight million followers, generating over 1.8 billion impressions and 1.35 billion video views. Highlights, short-form clips, player stories and locally produced content allow the league to remain part of the conversation throughout the year.Its approach to fan engagement also extends beyond the screen.BUDX NBA House, which moved from Mumbai to New Delhi in May this year, brings basketball together with music, fashion, celebrity appearances and entertainment. The format is particularly relevant in India, where the NBA's cultural appeal can reach audiences who may not necessarily follow the sport closely.The initiative has also found relevance beyond India, with elements of the experience informing the league's approach in other Asia-Pacific markets.There is, however, a distinction between building awareness and building a business. Social media numbers and event attendance offer encouraging signs, but converting occasional engagement into regular viewership, merchandise sales and long-term commercial partnerships remains the bigger test.Cricket continues to command the country's sporting attention, sponsorship money and broadcast market. The NBA also has to contend with a time-zone disadvantage and the challenge of developing a sizeable paying audience for a sport that still occupies a relatively small space in India's domestic sporting landscape.The league's India strategy, therefore, is built around connecting several businesses rather than relying on one. Broadcast distribution creates visibility, digital content sustains engagement, live experiences build communities, while merchandise and retail offer opportunities to monetise that relationship.The pieces are gradually falling into place. The question is whether they can come together to create something bigger.For the NBA, India's opportunity is not merely about getting more people to watch basketball. It is about making the league part of their sporting, cultural and consumer lives.
Article Summary: The NBA is expanding its merchandising partnership with Indian apparel company Suditi. The partnership will see the NBA open its first physical store in India in 2027. It is an important development for a league looking to take its relationship with fans beyond digital engagement and into everyday consumption.

Article Title: ‘He got greedy’: Ex-India captain's blunt take on Arshdeep Singh after four-wicket haul
Article Text:
India bowler Arshdeep Singh celebrates with teammate Virat Kohli (AP/PTI)

Jadeja impressed with Anshul Kamboj

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja has praised Arshdeep Singh's overall performance in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the first ODI in Auckland, but believes the left-arm pacer could have avoided an expensive finish to his spell.India began their five-match ODI series with a comfortable win at Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4. In a rain-interrupted contest reduced to 32 overs per side, New Zealand were bowled out for 185 before India chased down the revised target of 143 in just 22.4 overs. Virat Kohli led the chase with a fluent 74, while Shubman Gill contributed 37 as the duo stitched together a 113-run partnership. India eventually crossed the finish line with five wickets to spare and 56 deliveries remaining.With the ball, Arshdeep was India's leading wicket-taker, claiming four wickets in his 10 overs. However, his figures of 4/70 were inflated by an expensive final over in which New Zealand tailender Blair Tickner struck him for three sixes, taking 23 runs off the over.Assessing the pacer's performance, Jadeja felt Arshdeep had been impressive for most of his spell but allowed the opportunity to complete a five-wicket haul to influence his bowling towards the end."I would call him slightly greedy. He himself said that as well. If you remove his last over, he had dismissed four batters before that and had given 40-odd runs. He got slightly greedy for the fifth wicket in the last over," Jadeja said on Sony Sports Network.Arshdeep had himself admitted after the match that the fifth wicket would have been his favourite, indicating that he was keen to complete a five-wicket haul. Despite missing out on the milestone, his four-wicket effort placed him in an exclusive group of Indian fast bowlers to achieve the feat in an ODI in New Zealand, alongside Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami.Jadeja, however, stressed that the expensive final over should not overshadow what Arshdeep brings to India's bowling combination. He pointed to the value of having a left-arm fast bowler in an attack that already features Jasprit Bumrah, adding that the competition for places would only benefit the team."It happens. It's natural, but Arshdeep Singh is showing that he can play in ODIs as well, which I believe is a very good thing when a left-arm seamer gets added to this attack with (Jasprit) Bumrah. The competition has increased a lot, which is very good for India," Jadeja elaborated.Jadeja also reserved praise for Anshul Kamboj, who delivered an economical spell of 2/22 from his 10 overs and walked away with the Player of the Match award.The former India batter acknowledged that Kamboj had faced questions over his bowling during his Test debut against England in 2025, particularly regarding his pace and tendency to bowl no-balls. However, he felt the youngster had shown considerable improvement in Auckland.Jadeja also suggested that Kamboj's workload before the England assignment could have contributed to his struggles, pointing out that fatigue can affect a bowler's execution. His performance against New Zealand, according to Jadeja, reflected better pace, consistency and accuracy."He bowled extremely well. The vision everyone had was that he didn't have pace when he played in England and was bowling a lot of no-balls. I think he had come after playing a lot of cricket then. So a guy also gets tired. It's not that easy. Then he was playing for the first time, but the consistency and the slight increase in his pace he showed today (Wednesday), if we talk about the accuracy amongst the four bowlers, it's Anshul Kamboj," Jadeja added.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by five wickets in the first ODI in Auckland. Ajay Jadeja praised Arshdeep Singh's performance, but said he could have avoided expensive final over. Jadeja also praised Anshul Kamboj's bowling, saying he had shown improvement.

Article Title: ‘There was no place for mediocrity’: Venkatesh Iyer reveals Gautam Gambhir's dressing-room rule at KKR
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'There was no place for mediocrity': Iyer on Gambhir

Venkatesh Iyer has opened up about Gautam Gambhir's influence on Kolkata Knight Riders' (KKR) dressing room during their title-winning Indian Premier League (IPL) 2024 campaign, explaining how the former captain's presence helped establish a culture where players were always ready to attack.Gambhir, who led KKR to IPL titles in 2012 and 2014, returned to the franchise in 2024 as a mentor. His involvement proved important as the team went on to win another championship. He has since moved on from the franchise and is currently serving as India's head coach.Recalling the atmosphere in the KKR dugout, Iyer explained that the team's batting order was always prepared to take the field, even when the openers were still at the crease.“Our two openers, Narine and Salt, would go out to bat. Angkrish would sit there with his pads on. He just sat there, while the rest of us - me, Shreyas, Nitish Rana, Rinku Singh, Ramandeep, and Andre Russell - sat inside; all five of us would be padded up and ready to go from the second over itself,” Iyer said during a podcast with Aakash Chopra.Iyer said there was a sense of competition among the batters, with everyone eager to get an opportunity. However, Sunil Narine and Phil Salt often continued batting for several overs, keeping the waiting players on their toes.“There was this competition; anyone could go in at any moment, boss. We stayed ready, like literally. I, of course, saw it from my own perspective, but looking at them, they were like lions ready to go: ‘Just send us in, we’ll go and...’ And touch wood, Salt and Narine wouldn’t get out, they wouldn’t get out for a long time.”He also recalled how Gambhir would communicate the possible batting combinations from the dugout as the innings progressed. Players had to remain prepared because the instructions could change depending on the situation.“If they didn’t get out for three or four overs, GG sir from over there would say: ‘Angkrish, Venky is going next’, and I’d be ready. If they still didn’t get out for two more overs, he’d say from there: ‘It’s a left-right combination, Venky and Shreyas ’- and both of us would be ready. Then, if they stayed in even longer: ‘Call Russell, tell Russell’; but all of us were raring to go like that.”For Iyer, this was a different kind of dressing-room environment, with every batter looking forward to getting an opportunity to take the attack to the opposition.“That was the first time I witnessed something like that: give us an opportunity and we will go smash it."Iyer attributed the team's approach to the confidence Gambhir gave the players. According to him, the mentor's presence meant the batters were not worried about failure, but they also knew that the standards expected of them were high.“He was sitting right behind us. There was no fear. And there was no place for mediocrity in that dressing room. You can’t play a mediocre shot or a false stroke and come sit next to him. You can’t do that.”Iyer clarified that Gambhir did not need to introduce any formal rules to establish this atmosphere. His presence and expectations were enough to influence how the players approached their game.The franchise eventually lifted its third IPL trophy, adding to the titles it had won under Gambhir's captaincy in 2012 and 2014.
Article Summary: Venkatesh Iyer has opened up about Gautam Gambhir's influence on Kolkata Knight Riders' dressing room during their title-winning Indian Premier League (IPL) 2024 campaign. Iyer explained how the team's batting order was always prepared to take the field, even when the openers were still at the crease.

Article Title: ‘Too early for him’: Sachin Tendulkar's blunt verdict on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s leadership role at 15
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Sachin Tendulkar

Tendulkar names favourite captains

At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already achieved milestones that remain a distant dream for many cricketers throughout their careers. From finishing as the leading run-scorer in an Indian Premier League (IPL) season to smashing a match-winning century in the U-19 World Cup final to clinch the title, the teenager has made remarkable strides in a short span of time.However, his elevation to the role of East Zone vice-captain for the Duleep Trophy did not go down well with everyone. Among those who believe the youngster was handed a leadership responsibility too early is batting legend Sachin Tendulkar Although Tendulkar had not publicly questioned the selectors' decision at the time of the announcement, he shared his reservations during a Reddit Q&A session, suggesting that Sooryavanshi should focus on gaining more experience in red-ball cricket before taking on such responsibilities.Responding to a fan who asked for his views on the 15-year-old being entrusted with a leadership role, Tendulkar said: "I feel it's too early for him to become a vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy. We have to let him play more matches with the red ball and take one step at a time!"Sooryavanshi had featured in just eight red-ball matches for Bihar before being named East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan 's deputy. The decision meant he was preferred over Abhimanyu Easwaran, an experienced campaigner with more than 100 First-Class appearances.The East Zone selection committee subsequently clarified that the appointment was made with the youngster's development in mind and should not be interpreted as an indication of the pecking order within the squad.Sooryavanshi also got a taste of captaincy during the tournament when Kishan was forced to leave the field due to an injury. The teenager stepped in to lead the side and was involved in several important on-field decisions, including DRS calls. Videos of his involvement in those reviews also gained traction on social media.Meanwhile, Sooryavanshi has continued to strengthen his position in India's T20I setup, although he is yet to establish himself as a regular opener. The youngster faces competition for a place in the top three from established names such as Sanju Samson , Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan.During the same interaction, Tendulkar also reflected on his own stint as India's captain, describing the opportunity to lead the national side as a tremendous honour. However, he admitted that the position did not always give him complete control over team selection.Tendulkar, who made his international debut on November 15, 1989, before bringing the curtain down on his career on November 16, 2013, also spoke about the changes in the functioning of Indian cricket over the years."It was a great honour to lead the team as captain. However, I didn’t always have the freedom to pick my team entirely on my own. The BCCI today is a far more professional organisation than it was in the 1990s. Indian cricket also went through a particularly dark phase during that period," Tendulkar said.Asked to name his favourite captains, the former India skipper singled out Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni , acknowledging the impact both had on Indian cricket."As far as my favourite captains go, Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni would definitely be at the top of my list!!," Tendulkar said.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was named East Zone vice-captain for the Duleep Trophy. Sachin Tendulkar believes the 15-year-old should focus on red-ball cricket. The former India captain also named Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni as his favourite captains.

Article Title: Aussies turn to 'Mr Cricket': Former CSK coach joins Australia support staff for Ashes and 2027 World Cup
Article Text:

Mike Hussey was on Friday appointed as a consultant coach to the Australian team for next year's Ashes series against England and the 2027 ODI World Cup.The former Australia batter had revealed in August that England's new red-ball coach, Stephen Fleming, had informally approached him to take up the role of Test batting mentor. However, the 51-year-old turned down the offer and has instead decided to work with Australia as they look to address their batting struggles, which were exposed during their recent 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa.Hussey, who earned the nickname 'Mr Cricket' for his technical knowledge of the game, will also assist the Australian coaching staff during this month's home T20 series against England and the subsequent four-Test series against New Zealand.His role will extend beyond next year's assignments, with Hussey also set to work with Australia at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket will feature, and the 2028 T20 World Cup."I am extremely excited about being a part of the team in a more formal and meaningful role in the coming years," said Hussey, who represented Australia in more than 300 international matches across all formats."This team has achieved so much in recent times, to which I hope I can add value to the coaching and playing groups ahead of what will be an exciting and challenging period."Hussey has considerable coaching experience, having worked with both Australia and England. He was part of England's coaching setup when they won the T20 World Cup in 2022 and served as Chennai Super Kings' long-time batting coach under Fleming in the Indian Premier League. He also coached Welsh Fire in this year's edition of The Hundred."Mike has been a highly valued part of our staff in the past and brings a considerable skill set which is complementary to the coaches and players," said Australia head coach Andrew McDonald."Not only is his expertise as a player and coach across multiple formats, competitions, countries invaluable, so are his qualities as a person."
Article Summary: Mike Hussey appointed as a consultant coach to the Australian team. Hussey will work with Australia for next year's Ashes series against England and the 2027 ODI World Cup. The 51-year-old will also assist the Australian coaching staff during this month's home T20 series againstEngland and the subsequent Test series against New Zealand.

Article Text:
Virat Kohli

India fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh has praised the team's sharpness and commitment on the field following their victory in the opening ODI against New Zealand, pointing to the collective effort of the fielding unit in restricting the hosts to 185.India began the five-match series with a five-wicket win via the DLS method in a rain-interrupted contest at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday. Ghosh felt the team's performance in the field, particularly their catching, ground fielding and overall intensity, complemented the bowlers' efforts in keeping New Zealand's total under control.Speaking to reporters on the eve of the second ODI in Hamilton, Ghosh expressed satisfaction with the way the players backed up the bowling attack with their fielding contributions."We did well in the first ODI. We took some good catches, picked up wickets and backed it up with excellent ground fielding. The intensity was very good. When you restrict the opposition to around 180, it reflects not just good bowling but also quality fielding," Ghosh said.Among the standout moments in the series opener were Virat Kohli 's spectacular catch and Rohit Sharma 's sharp run-out. Both senior batters made significant contributions in the field, with Ghosh attributing their efforts to their ability to anticipate situations and read the game quickly.Explaining Kohli 's brilliance, the fielding coach pointed to the batter's extensive experience in the cover and point positions, which allows him to judge the direction and movement of the ball more effectively."I think anticipation is extremely important. The more time you spend in a particular fielding position, the better you become at reading the game. Virat has fielded at cover and point countless times, so he knows the trajectory and path of the ball, as well as how it is likely to travel after impact. He reads the situation slightly earlier than others, and you can see that in his execution," he said.Ghosh also broke down Rohit's contribution to the run-out, explaining how the Indian batter had already begun moving towards square leg after anticipating where the ball was likely to travel. That early movement helped him execute the dismissal with precision."As far as Rohit is concerned, I think he anticipated that the ball would go towards square leg during that run-out. He wasn't moving straight; he was already shifting slightly towards square leg. That early anticipation allowed him to execute the skill perfectly. The more familiar you become with a particular position, the quicker you are able to anticipate what is going to happen. That's what makes the difference," he added.The fielding coach also spoke about the difficulties players encounter while adjusting to different playing conditions during overseas tours. Varying ground dimensions, colder weather and unfamiliar boundary placements can all influence a fielder's positioning and movement.According to Ghosh, understanding the dimensions of a ground and making the correct initial movement are particularly important, as they help players cover more ground and reduce the angles available to opposition batters."When you travel to different countries, adapting to new conditions is always a challenge. The ground dimensions vary, the weather can be cold, and these are aspects we regularly discuss in the dressing room. In terms of ground dimensions, when you field in a particular position, observing the batters and understanding where the boundary rope is becomes important. Your first step is crucial because it allows you to cut down the angles and cover the ground more effectively.We constantly work on that initial movement," he said.Ghosh further stressed that adapting to changing environments is an essential part of international cricket and requires players to maintain the right approach, irrespective of whether they are training or competing."That is part of the challenge of international cricket. You travel to different countries, encounter different conditions and have to adapt accordingly. With optional training sessions, it ultimately comes down to your mindset. I always emphasise the importance of having the right mindset, both individually and as a group," he concluded.India will take on New Zealand in the second ODI at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Saturday. While the hosts will be eager to draw level, India will look to build on their opening victory and extend their advantage in the series.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by five wickets in the first ODI in Auckland on Wednesday. fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh has praised the team's commitment on the field. Ghosh also praised Virat Kohli's spectacular catch and Rohit Sharma's sharp run-out. India face New Zealand in the second ODI at Hamilton on Saturday.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.China topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze.Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. Star javelin thrower Sumit Antil led an Indian 1-2-3 finish in the men's F42-44/61-64 combined event . Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again

Sumit Antil and Pranav Soorma (ANI/PTI Photo)

Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.

Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa secured bronze in men's doubles para table tennis MD4.India's tally stood at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with the country fourth in the standings. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

Article Title: 53 red cards in one match! Brazil football game sets bizarre world record after mass brawl

53 red cards in one match! Brazil football game sets bizarre world record after mass brawl
