Football witnessed an extraordinary scene in Brazil after a mass brawl during an under-20s match resulted in 53 dismissals, setting a new world record for the most red cards issued in a single game.The unprecedented incident took place during a local U20 semifinal in Minas Gerais on Sunday, when Mamoré were leading Uberlândia 3-1 in the second half. Celebrations following Mamoré's third goal triggered a confrontation that soon escalated into a mass fight involving players and officials from both sides.According to the referee's report, Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto sent off 40 players and eight members of the coaching and support staff in the aftermath of the brawl. Three players had already received red cards earlier in the contest. Two Uberlândia board members were also dismissed, taking the overall tally to 53.The figure surpasses the previous Guinness World Record of 36 red cards, set during an Argentinian fifth-division fixture between Atlético Claypole and Victoriano Arenas in February 2011.The referee's report provided details of how the chaotic scenes unfolded.Mamoré player Davi allegedly taunted the opposition bench while celebrating his team's third goal, prompting Uberlândia goalkeeping coach Paulo Sérgio Dias Dos Santos to enter the pitch and confront him.What followed was a widespread altercation involving players and members of the staff, leaving the referee with little choice but to take disciplinary action against those involved.The situation also reportedly took a threatening turn, with Drosghic Modesto alleging that several individuals directed death threats and other threats of violence towards him. A police report was subsequently filed in connection with the incident, according to the referee's account.The match was stopped for 40 minutes before eventually being abandoned as the situation could not be brought under control.The trouble did not end with the on-field confrontation. Following the match, allegations emerged that Uberlândia officials had damaged equipment belonging to Mamoré. Members of the Mamoré team were also accused of vandalising the home dressing room.The incident has now set a remarkable new benchmark in football's disciplinary history, with the 53 dismissals eclipsing the previous record by a considerable margin.
Article Summary: A mass brawl during an under-20s match resulted in 53 dismissals. The unprecedented incident took place during a local U20 semifinal in Minas Gerais. 40 players and eight members of the coaching and support staff were sent off in the aftermath of the brawl.

Article Title: Lamine Yamal surpasses Kylian Mbappé to become Champions League’s highest-scoring teenager with 14 goals
Article Text:
Soccer Football - UEFA Champions League - FC Barcelona v Aston Villa - Spotify Camp Nou, Barcelona, Spain - November 3, 2026 FC Barcelona's Lamine Yamal celebrates scoring their first goal REUTERS/Albert Gea

Yamal moves past Mbappé with Barcelona goal against Aston Villa

Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, left, duels for the ball with Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe during the Spanish Super Cup final soccer match at King Abdullah Sports City Stadium in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, Sunday, Jan. 11, 2026. (AP Photo/Altaf Qadri)

A Champions League career already filled with records

Yamal's form gives Barcelona another attacking threat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lamine Yamal has moved ahead of Kylian Mbappé in the Champions League record books, becoming the competition’s highest-scoring teenager after finding the net in Barcelona’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa. The 19-year-old’s latest milestone came during a commanding performance by the LaLiga champions at Spotify Camp Nou, adding another record to a European career that began before he had even turned 17.Yamal opened the scoring in the seventh minute on Tuesday, November 3, capitalising on an Aston Villa mistake before bending the ball past goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. It was his 14th Champions League goal, taking him beyond Mbappé’s previous teenage record of 13.The Barcelona forward reached that total in 37 appearances in the competition, while Mbappé achieved his 13-goal teenage tally in exactly 23 appearances. Mbappé, who now plays for Real Madrid, has since gone on to score 72 Champions League goals in his career. The Frenchman had held the teenage record before Yamal surpassed it at Spotify Camp Nou.Barcelona went on to win 3-0, with Raphinha scoring twice after Yamal’s opener.The result ended Villa’s unbeaten start to the League Phase and provisionally lifted the Spanish champions into second place in the standings.The latest achievement adds to a series of age-related milestones Yamal has collected since making his European debut. He remains the youngest player to start a match in the Champions League proper, having made his first full appearance against Porto at just 16 years and 83 days.He is also the youngest player to score and assist in the same Champions League match, as well as the youngest to find the net in a semi-final. His scoring record is particularly notable for the number of goals he had accumulated before reaching successive birthdays: five before turning 18 and 11 before turning 19.Yamal is no longer the youngest player to appear in the competition's knockout stages, however, after Max Dowman took that distinction earlier this year. That record does not diminish the scale of his scoring achievements, which have now taken him beyond Mbappé's teenage total.Yamal's record-breaking goal is part of an impressive start to the 2026-27 campaign. Across 15 appearances in all competitions, he has scored 13 goals and provided 11 assists, giving Barcelona a consistent source of goals and creativity.His performances have also brought individual recognition. Yamal finished third in last week's Ballon d'Or voting, behind Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane and Mbappé, who placed second.At 19, he has already surpassed a Champions League scoring mark previously held by one of the competition's most prolific modern forwards. Mbappé's overall tally continues to grow at Real Madrid, but the teenage record now belongs to Yamal.
Article Summary: Lamine Yamal has become the Champions League's highest-scoring teenager. The 19-year-old scored in Barcelona's 3-0 win over Aston Villa on November 3. It was his 14th Champions League goal, overtaking Kylian Mbappé's previous record of 13.

But alongside the success, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner has also found himself at the centre of several controversies, both on and off the pitch.As the 41-year-old announced his decision to retire from international football after the November 2026 break, his final months in a Portugal shirt were also marked by a public fallout with coach Jorge Jesus. That episode added another chapter to a career in which Ronaldo's actions, comments and conduct have repeatedly made headlines.One of the most recent controversies came during Portugal's September 2026 international camp. Ronaldo was an unused substitute in the team's 2-1 Nations League win over Norway on September 27, despite warming up during the match.Reports subsequently emerged that the forward had left the camp after a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus over his playing time.Ronaldo was said to be unhappy because he believed an agreement had been reached regarding his involvement.The episode prompted an investigation by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF). On October 19, the Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary body handed him a 30-day suspension and a fine of 255 euros for leaving the national team camp without permission.The controversy came just weeks before Ronaldo announced his international retirement.
